goal: Turn the reserved inert AskSayre dock into a real, collapsible right-hand Ask Sayre chat panel mounted across the Technical, Product, and Onboarding views: it auto-attaches the current view + selected node as scope, posts questions through the existing core proxy to CH-03's chat routes, renders live progress and markdown answers driven by CH-05's pinned chat.turn.* WebSocket events, and lets a citation chip select and zoom the cited Folder/File node on the canvas. The entire diff is confined to apps/web/.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Ticket AC1. Submitting a non-blank question calls ChatClient.postTurn against POST /api/core/chat/conversations/:id/turns with body exactly { question, scope: { view, anchorNodeId }, idempotencyKey } and appends the returned userTurn plus the pending assistantTurn to the transcript in ordinal order. No other field (org id, repository id, user id) is ever placed in the body.

Ticket AC1. The conversation is created lazily exactly once per workspace session via POST /api/core/chat/conversations (body {}), reused by every later turn, and reset (transcript cleared, socket closed) when the repository/ref scope changes. A second concurrent ask never creates a second conversation.

Ticket AC1. chat.turn.progress pushes for the active conversation and a known turnId promote that assistant turn from 'pending' to 'running' and render an ordered progress ticker; a 'tool_call' line renders the tool name and detail in the quiet mono style, a 'status' line renders only its detail.

Ticket AC1. chat.turn.completed collapses the ticker and renders, in order, the markdown answer as safe block elements, the citation chip row, and the metrics footer formatted as 'N context nodes · X tokens · R× less than full repo'.

Ticket AC2. citationTarget(citation, { view, knownFeatureIds }) resolves: kind 'file'|'folder' -> select-node on resolvedNodeId ?? nodeId; kind 'feature' in the product view with a known feature id -> select-feature; kind 'feature'|'ticket' otherwise with a non-null resolvedNodeId -> select-node; anything else -> none. The panel dispatches select-node through selection.selectNode when the current view is 'technical' and selection.openNodeInTechnicalView otherwise, and select-feature through selection.selectFeature — the same mechanism DependenciesModule already uses — so the cited node becomes the canvas focus and is zoomed to.

Ticket AC2. A citation that resolves to 'none' renders as a non-interactive <span> chip carrying the 'not on canvas' hint and dispatches nothing. The accepted citation kind set is exactly file|folder|feature|ticket; any other kind is parsed to 'unknown' and can only resolve to 'none', so no code path in apps/web/app/workspace/chat/ can select or render a Function or Class node on canvas.

Ticket AC3. The scope chip above the input shows the current view and, when a node is selected, that node's label; it is a real dismissible button. Dismissing clears only anchorNodeId (the view stays), and the anchor re-attaches when a different node is subsequently selected.

Ticket AC3. The scope object sent in postTurn is byte-for-byte the chip's current state: { view: <current ViewId>, anchorNodeId: <selected node id or null after dismissal> }, and the turn stores that scope so a retry re-sends the same one.

Ticket AC4. With no turns, the panel renders the empty state whose per-view suggested prompt is a real <button type="button"> ('technical' -> 'Explain this folder', 'product' -> 'What feature does this belong to?', 'onboarding' -> 'What should I start first?'); activating it submits that prompt as a turn.

Ticket AC4. When providerConfigurationStatus(providerSettings().settings.generation) is not 'configured', the panel renders the provider-unconfigured notice, disables the input with a stated reason, and offers a labeled button that opens the 'providers' settings section via navigation.openSettings('providers'). Any failure to read provider settings (including the 403 a member receives) resolves to 'unknown' and does NOT block the input.

Ticket AC4. chat.turn.error renders an inline error turn showing the server's sanitized message and a 'Try again' button; activating it re-posts that turn's stored question and scope with a NEW idempotency key and appends a fresh user + pending assistant pair.

Ticket AC5. On provider mount with an existing conversation and on every (re)connect of the chat socket, GET /api/core/chat/conversations/:id reconciles the transcript by turn id: the Postgres status/content/citations/metrics/error win, no turn id is duplicated, no locally known turn is dropped, and locally accumulated progress lines survive.

Ticket AC6. The composer is a <form> containing a labeled <input id="ask-sayre-input"> so Enter submits natively; the dock toggle, the scope chip, every drawable citation chip, the suggested-prompt buttons, and the retry button are all real <button type="button"> elements with accessible names, reachable by Tab and activated by Enter.
Ticket AC6. The progress ticker is rendered inside a container carrying aria-live="polite" (and role="status") so appended progress lines are announced without stealing focus.

Ticket AC7. The panel renders only server-delivered data. No module under apps/web/app/workspace/chat/ performs graph traversal, node-stripping, or any permission-like predicate; the only client-side filtering is the closed presentational citation-kind enum and canvas drawability, both of which are rendering decisions, not authorization.

The 'ask-sayre' entry is registered in apps/web/app/workspace/askSayreRegistry.ts following the moduleRegistry conventions (id/title/defaultOpen/capability/availability plus a dedicated renderer map), every registered id has exactly one renderer, no new canonical data shape is introduced, and AskSayreDock renders the panel with the correct view-scoped chip and suggested prompt for each of 'technical', 'product', and 'onboarding'.

The markdown answer is rendered through parseAnswerBlocks into React text nodes only: no dangerouslySetInnerHTML anywhere in apps/web/app/workspace/chat/, and no anchor/href is ever constructed from answer, citation, tool, or detail text.

The dock is collapsible: expanded it renders the panel with a labeled toggle carrying aria-expanded="true" and aria-controls="ask-sayre-panel"; collapsed it renders only a slim rail whose single labeled button carries aria-expanded="false", and the panel body is not rendered.

edgeCases.text: A duplicate chat.turn.progress (same turnId and same seq delivered twice) is applied exactly once — the ticker shows one line, lastProgressSeq is unchanged by the repeat.
Out-of-order progress (seq 3 then seq 2 for the same turnId) drops the lower seq; the rendered ticker order is strictly increasing and never rewrites already-rendered lines.
Gapped progress (seq 1 then seq 4) renders both lines, invents no filler line for 2 and 3, and does not stall or buffer waiting for the gap to close.
A chat.turn.progress arriving AFTER chat.turn.completed or chat.turn.error for the same turnId is ignored: the collapsed ticker is not reopened, the answer is not replaced, and status stays terminal.
Any chat.turn.* push whose conversationId is not the active conversation is ignored entirely — no turn is created, mutated, or reordered.
Any chat.turn.* push whose turnId is not already in the transcript is ignored — the client never fabricates a phantom turn from a push alone.

Terminal events carry NO seq per the pinned contract; if a terminal event nevertheless carries one, the client ignores that field, never advances lastProgressSeq from it, and a later progress event is still compared only against the progress-derived lastProgressSeq.
A second terminal event for the same turn (completed after error, error after completed, or completed twice) is ignored — the first terminal event wins and the rendered turn does not flip.

The gateway WebSocket is unavailable or never connects (browserRealtimeUrl returns null, construction throws, or the socket closes before open): the panel enters the REST-only degraded path, polls GET /api/core/chat/conversations/:id every CHAT_DEGRADED_POLL_INTERVAL_MS while any assistant turn is non-terminal, stops after CHAT_DEGRADED_POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS, and shows a visible note that live progress is unavailable plus a 'Check again' button. Turns still complete.

Reconnect mid-turn: while the socket is down the turn completes server-side; on reconnect the REST reconcile adopts the completed row without duplicating the assistant turn, without losing it, and without re-appending the user turn.
chat.turn.completed with citations: [] renders the answer and the metrics footer and omits the citation row entirely (no empty container, no placeholder chip).
A 'feature' or 'ticket' citation with resolvedNodeId: null renders as a non-interactive chip with the 'not on canvas' hint and dispatches no selection.

A citation whose kind is a value the client does not draw (anything outside file|folder|feature|ticket, including 'function' or 'class') is parsed to kind 'unknown', kept in the citation list so the evidence is not silently dropped, rendered non-interactive with the 'not on canvas' hint, and can never produce a selection.

metrics.baselineTokens is 0, or ratio is 0/negative/non-finite: the footer renders 'N context nodes · X tokens' and omits the 'R× less than full repo' clause. The client never divides baselineTokens by tokensUsed — it only formats the server-supplied ratio — so no divide-by-zero is reachable.
metrics is missing, not an object, or has a non-numeric/non-finite field: parseChatMetrics returns null, no footer renders, and the answer and citations still render.

chat.turn.error with code 'chat.mcp_unauthorized' — including the case of a turn that sat in queue backlog past the 300s ephemeral-credential TTL — renders the same inline error turn with a working 'Try again' affordance; no credential, provider, or queue detail is displayed.
Submitting while this conversation's own turn is pending or running: the input is disabled with a stated reason, and a programmatic submit performs no request and appends no turn.
An empty or whitespace-only question performs no request, appends no turn, leaves the field contents untouched, keeps the submit button disabled, and shows a role="status" hint.

POST /chat/conversations or POST .../turns fails (400, 502, network, malformed JSON, contract violation): an inline composer error with a retry is shown, the question text is preserved for editing, and no phantom user or assistant turn is left in the transcript.

A malformed WebSocket frame (non-JSON, non-object, missing/wrongly-typed conversationId, turnId, seq, kind, ts, answer, code, or message) makes parseChatGatewayMessage return null; the frame is discarded without throwing and without touching transcript state.

The answer markdown contains raw HTML, a <script> tag, or a javascript: URL: it is rendered as literal text through React text nodes; no HTML is injected and no anchor is constructed from answer content.

The repository or ref scope changes mid-conversation: the transcript is cleared, the chat socket is unsubscribed and closed, degraded polling stops, and no turn from the previous scope remains rendered.

A question longer than CHAT_QUESTION_MAX_CHARACTERS (8000, CH-03's limit) is capped by the input's maxLength; if the server still rejects it, the 400 surfaces through EC-19's inline composer error rather than a thrown render.

Session expiry — a 401 from any chat REST call, or a gateway 'error' frame with code 'unauthenticated', or a socket close with code 4401 — stops polling and the socket and defers to the workspace's existing session-expired handling rather than showing a chat-specific message or retrying in a loop.

The active view changes while a turn is pending: the pending turn keeps the scope it was posted with (its stored turn.scope), while the composer's chip immediately reflects the new view for the next question.

A citation chip is activated while the current view is 'product' or 'onboarding' and resolves to select-node: the panel uses selection.openNodeInTechnicalView so the Technical Tree becomes active and the node is selected there, rather than selecting an id the current canvas cannot draw.
